item.text: {"rubric":[{"claim_id":"c1","claim_type":"core","weight":35,"statement":"`Module.batch` constructs its work queue as `(self, example.inputs())` for each item, so it does not queue the original full `Example` objects.","span_ids":["s1"]},{"claim_id":"c2","claim_type":"core","weight":25,"statement":"When `return_failed_examples=True`, `Module.batch` returns the `failed_examples` produced by `Parallel.forward`, and `Parallel.forward` populates that list by appending `exec_pairs[failed_idx][1]` for each failed index.","span_ids":["s1","s2"]},{"claim_id":"c3","claim_type":"core","weight":30,"statement":"The loss of labels or other non-input fields is expected from this implementation, because failed batch items are returned from the already-transformed `example.inputs()` payloads rather than from the original examples.","span_ids":["s1","s2"]},{"claim_id":"c4","claim_type":"supporting","weight":10,"statement":"The failure-path test shows non-aborting batch behavior: the results list keeps successful outputs with `None` in the failed slot, and the returned failed item is checked only via its failing input value (`42`) plus the captured `ValueError`.","span_ids":["s3"]}],"evidence":[{"span_id":"s1","path":"dspy/primitives/module.py","start_line":297,"end_line":314},{"span_id":"s2","path":"dspy/predict/parallel.py","start_line":113,"end_line":123},{"span_id":"s3","path":"tests/predict/test_parallel.py","start_line":169,"end_line":196}]}
